analysis: Both units are head_text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 603-783 and 784-1017). They are documentation-only: no executable code, config, or workflow changes are in the supplied text, so no concrete security regression can be demonstrated from these units. The changelog describes v0.9.10 candidate behavior touching the threat model areas TB-002, TB-009, TB-011 and T-052..T-058: App Attest dead-key rotation (budget of 1/hour and 4/24h per machine, 6h backoff after the third invalidKey failure, with rotations never revoking or denying serving), optional untrusted diagnostics on ready replies outside the signed transcript, an admin /app-attest/diagnostics endpoint, APNs retry hourly, model-demand public stats with k-anonymity suppression (20 requests / 3 accounts, 1h delay), and live model switching. These claims are consistent with the existing threat model, which already treats diagnostics as untrusted metadata. The changelog states that the rotation and diagnostic paths do not affect authorization, but the actual implementation (coordinator/appattest/service, protocol/app_attest_deep_diagnostic.go, rotation admission, public demand aggregation, model-switch routing fence) was not supplied. A later pass with the code diffs should verify the following: rotation re-enrollment passes full attestation, receipt, build qualification and assertion checks; the rotation budget cannot be bypassed via machine merges; the public model-demand suppression cannot be defeated by subtraction; and the switch fence prevents dispatch before refreshed capacity. No threat-model gaps are evident from the changelog alone; a threat model update note for diagnostics and the new public demand stats may be warranted if the code is large. Coverage limit: the claims were not verified against source.
